Subject: Intermittent large-packet drops after private cutover

Hi Kimberly / Vanessa —

We completed the private connectivity cutover to Redwood yesterday evening. Since then we see intermittent failures from our app hosts to external third-party APIs over the private egress path: large outbound packets (around 1500B) sometimes get silently dropped and TCP sessions stall (retransmits spike). The failures are bursty, ~5-10/min for a handful of hosts.

Attached is a short traceroute + MTR log from one affected host (20280612-northbridge-trace.txt). Key facts:
- Only happens on flows that exceed ~1200B. Smaller requests are fine.
- Issue appears on the egress path that traverses the on-prem firewall -> transit device -> Redwood private gateway.
- We’ve already validated firewall rules look normal and the ISP path shows no CRCs.

Can Redwood ops take a look? We can jump on a call but wanted to share traces first.

Thanks,
Sam

Quick update after an initial look:

Findings so far (from gateway telemetry and NAT counters):
- Egress MTU at the Redwood gateway reports 1500, no obvious fragment drops in kernel counters.
- NAT engine shows short bursts of high ephemeral port reuse for the Northbridge source prefix; peak ephemeral usage ~ 96% on a single worker (see attached 20280614-ephemeral-counters.csv).
- We observed flow churn where multiple simultaneous outbound connections use the same 4-tuple and get mapped unpredictably; that can lead to packets being dropped when a path asymmetry exists and the return takes a different SNAT worker.

Hypothesis: some combination of SNAT port sparsity + asymmetric return path is causing state mismatch and large-packet retransmits. Large packets may exacerbate the issue (differences in segmentization and handling by middleboxes).

Immediate mitigations to try:
1) On our gateway: preferentially stick the Northbridge prefix to a single SNAT worker (reduces cross-worker collisions).
2) Ask Northbridge to enable MSS clamping to ~1400 on the firewall to avoid fragmentation across any middlebox.
3) Temporarily expand ephemeral port range on either side (if possible) to reduce reuse.

Connor/Marissa — can you capture a tcpdump with 'tcp[13] & 0x04 != 0 or tcp[13] & 0x02 != 0' for affected src IPs and include sequence numbers so we can correlate SYN/SYN-ACK flows?

—Vanessa

Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drops after private cutover

Captured sample tcpdump attached (20280613-northbridge-tcpdump.pcapng). Early observations:
- I see several SYNs from host 10.22.13.45 -> remote:443 with SYN-ACKs returned, but occasionally our gateway forwards a different ephemeral mapping on the SYN-ACK path. Sequence/ACK numbers align with asymmetric mapping, causing our NAT lookup to miss and drop subsequent segments.
- There are a handful of IP fragments present when MSS > 1400; fragments are sometimes dropped mid-path by the ISP device (we see ICMP frag-needed suppressed in some flows).

Commands I ran:
- conntrack -S (showing conntrack high-water spikes)
- ss -tnp state syn-recv
- ethtool -k on egress interface (no GSO/GRO offloads disabled unexpectedly)

Recommendations:
1) Enable strict SNAT affinitized mapping for the Northbridge prefix (stickiness). I can push a limited config change and roll back if it causes issues.
2) Coordinate MSS clamp to 1400 on the Northbridge firewall.
3) If frag-needed ICMPs are suppressed upstream, enable per-flow MSS or segment at the application edge.

I can make the SNAT stickiness change now if Kimberly approves.

—Connor

We applied a temporary MSS clamp to 1400 on the external firewall and expanded the ephemeral range on the app tier yesterday evening. We saw an immediate reduction in failures (from 6-8/min down to 0-1/min). We also confirmed the ISP was dropping some fragments (they denied ICMP in some cases).

We would like Redwood to apply the SNAT stickiness change for the Northbridge prefix during a maintenance window tomorrow morning (window: 2028-06-15 02:00-03:00 UTC). Can you schedule that and confirm a rollback plan? Also requesting a short post-mortem with recommended long-term fixes (per-prefix SNAT pools or VNAT, and guidance on MSS/Pmtu handling).

Attaching the pcap we pulled during the peak (20280613-northbridge-tcpdump.pcapng) and the ephemeral counters CSV.
